title: queen-bee status command: byte-parity vs bee.mjs status --json + host-real 5ms bench gate (D5 proof)
action: Assemble `queen-bee status [--json]` from the readers ported in rust-port-13/14, reproducing bee.mjs buildStatus (bee.mjs:724) + renderStatusText exactly (field order, nesting, null-vs-absent, degraded flags, the human text renderer). PROOF IS TWO-PART: (1) BYTE-PARITY — bee-parity today dispatches ONLY `--self-check` (crates/bee-parity/src/main.rs:34-43, self-parity + seeded mutation, which is rust-port-4's verify) and its runner is hardcoded to the mjs leg. ADD a SECOND `--status-check` arm — never repurpose `--self-check`, whose rust-port-4 verify must still pass afterwards: run `node .bee/bin/bee.mjs status --json` and `queen-bee status --json` over the SAME cloned host-real fixture store (queen-bench --generate) in self-sufficient temp roots outside the repo, diff stdout byte-for-byte after the declared volatile allowlist only, and diff post-run store trees (excluded set {.bee/logs/**, .bee/cache/**, .bee/tmp/**}); include a seeded-mutation negative control proving the comparison still detects a difference, and assert BOTH inner exits are 0 (two identical failures are not parity). `--status-check` ALSO runs the text leg (no --json) and diffs the rendered human output, so truth 3 has a real instrument. (2) BENCH GATE — queen-bench already has --generate/--self-test/--check (crates/queen-bench/src/main.rs:27-37) and resolves the queen-bee binary via current_exe or --bin-path; extend `--check` to also measure `queen-bee status --json` on the pinned host-real fixture (min 50 runs, spawn-inclusive p95, --budget-ms default 5) and record the node baseline for the same command in the JSON report. BINARY FRESHNESS: the verify builds the whole workspace FIRST — neither queen-bench nor bee-parity depends on queen-bee as a cargo dependency, so `cargo run -p <x>` alone would silently measure a stale target/release/queen-bee and report a green gate for a status command it never built. TWO ESCAPES, both [BLOCKED] with evidence rather than a weakened proof: (a) if 5ms proves unreachable for status on the host-real fixture, do NOT shrink the fixture — report the measured p95 plus a profile so the orchestrator can log a per-command budget supersession; (b) if the parity leg cannot reach zero diff because of genuine non-determinism the allowlist should not cover, report the exact differing fields rather than widening the allowlist to make it pass.

truths: cargo build --release of the whole workspace precedes both proofs in the verify (no stale-binary green)
bee-parity --status-check reports zero diff for BOTH the --json and the text leg between bee.mjs status and queen-bee status on the grown host-real fixture, with both inner exits 0
the seeded-mutation negative control runs PER LEG (json and text) and is detected on each — a text-leg-only normalization leak must not stay invisible
all volatility handling for --status-check lives in the ONE declared allowlist — no normalization inside diff helpers or the tree comparison
queen-bench --check gates queen-bee status --json at p95 under the budget on the pinned grown fixture, node baseline recorded alongside

the bench report states BOTH cold-cache and warm-cache status percentiles explicitly (the review-git cache from rust-port-14 makes them differ by ~10ms) — reporting only the warm number is not an honest D5 result

the parity legs tolerate the additive .bee/runtime/review-git-cache.json artifact by excluding .bee/runtime/** as a whole-path exclusion beside {.bee/logs/**, .bee/cache/**, .bee/tmp/**}, since the rust leg writes it and the mjs leg never does

new --status-check arm (json + text legs, per-leg negative control) beside the untouched --self-check
status bench added to --check, cold and warm cache percentiles, node baseline

trace.outcome: queen-bee status ported and proven byte-identical to the frozen bee.mjs oracle across SIX legs (--json, human text, and --json --lanes-full, each over a plain and an enriched store shape), with per-leg seeded-mutation controls asserted on the stdout diff specifically. Rework round closed the judge's declared-deviations-justified finding: serde_json preserve_order silently aliases Map::remove to swap_remove workspace-wide, which had changed the semantics of two pre-existing call sites — build_lane_rows (status's lanes block) and rebuild_handoff_projection (.bee/HANDOFF.json, a D3 store file). Both fixed to shift_remove/explicit composition, the whole workspace swept (two remaining .remove( calls are order-irrelevant and annotated), and both fixes proven red-first by reverting them. Proving the first uncovered a SECOND, independent D3 break: mjs laneRecordFrom emits defaultLaneRecord's key order (schema_version, feature, mode, phase) while the port emitted the State struct's (schema_version, phase, feature, mode) — invisible until the harness stopped inheriting CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and gained a --lanes-full leg. Byte-level HANDOFF.json parity plus a key-order sentinel added to projection_parity.rs, whose pre-existing parsed-Value assertions were order-blind by construction. queen-bench --check now carries per-command budgets: ping keeps D5's 5 ms spawn floor (p95 1.425), status carries its own 70 ms from supersession e119fc8b (warm p95 50.979, cold p95 53.493, node 179.188), each gate naming its own budget in the report.

deviations.kind: out-of-glob edit with workspace-wide blast radius
deviations.what: Enabled the serde_json `preserve_order` feature on crates/bee-core, crates/queen-bee and crates/queen-bench Cargo.toml. THIS IS NOT A PURELY ADDITIVE FLAG: in serde_json 1.0.150 (src/map.rs:156-165) `Map::remove` is `#[cfg(feature = "preserve_order")] return self.swap_remove(key)`, and swap_remove's own docs say it 'perturbs the position of what used to be the last element'. Enabling the feature therefore silently changed the SEMANTICS of every pre-existing `serde_json::Map::remove` call in the workspace. (An earlier version of this deviation record claimed 'no bee-core SOURCE was edited; the change is one additive cargo feature' -- that claim was false in effect and is retracted here.)
deviations.why: Byte-parity (D3) is impossible without the feature. JSON.stringify emits JS INSERTION order; a default serde_json::Map is a BTreeMap that re-emits ALPHABETICALLY. That breaks constructed blocks (mjs writes {candidates, open_sessions, high_risk_unreviewed}; a BTreeMap emits {candidates, high_risk_unreviewed, open_sessions}) and, worse, destroys the on-disk file order of every pass-through object status echoes verbatim -- models, handoff, gates, commands -- which nothing on the queen-bee side could reconstruct.
deviations.blast_radius: Two pre-existing call sites were silently affected, both now fixed to the order-preserving `shift_remove`: (1) crates/bee-core/src/state.rs build_lane_rows -- `map.remove("workers")` on a serialized lane row, feeding status's `lanes` block; (2) crates/bee-core/src/state_projection.rs rebuild_handoff_projection -- `projected.remove(key)` over five mailbox-only keys of a map written straight to .bee/HANDOFF.json, a D3-covered store file whose mjs counterpart drops the same keys with order-preserving `delete`. A full workspace sweep for `.remove(`/`remove_entry(` found only two other hits, both order-irrelevant and now annotated in code: backlog.rs:170 is Vec::remove (already order-preserving, not a Map) and decisions.rs:174 is std HashMap::remove whose output order comes from a separate `order` vector, never from map iteration. rust-port-17's new write paths (claims.rs, reservations.rs, holds.rs) and new queen-bee hooks were included in the sweep and carry no Map::remove.
deviations.proven_by: HANDOFF.json: crates/bee-core/tests/projection_parity.rs now byte-compares the mjs-oracle-produced and rust-produced files (assert_projected_bytes_identical) plus an explicit key-order assertion -- the pre-existing assert_eq! on parsed Values could NEVER have caught this, because serde_json::Map is an IndexMap under preserve_order and IndexMap's PartialEq ignores order. Lane rows: bee-parity --status-check gained a pinned session id (so buildLaneSummary resolves an ACTIVE lane and serializes a full lane record) and a third `--lanes-full` leg, giving six legs diffed against the frozen mjs. RED-FIRST VERIFIED BOTH WAYS, quoted in the report: reverting state_projection.rs to `remove` fails with `mjs key order: [kind, written_at, cell, writer_session]` vs `rust key order: [kind, writer_session, written_at, cell]`; reverting the lane-row build fails the enriched/json and enriched/json+lanes-full legs.
deviations.scope: crates/bee-core/* is outside this cell's original files glob (crates/queen-bee/*, crates/bee-parity/*, crates/queen-bench/*). The coordinator confirmed bee-core was free after rust-port-17 released its reservations; the paths were reserved under Carl before any edit.

deviations.kind: bug found by the new coverage (bee-core source fix)
deviations.what: Rewrote crates/bee-core/src/state.rs build_lane_rows to emit lane records in defaultLaneRecord's key order (schema_version, feature, mode, phase, approved_gates, summary, next_action, created_at, then record-only extras, then bound_sessions) instead of serializing the shared `State` struct and deleting `workers`.
deviations.why: A genuine D3 byte-compatibility break, distinct from the preserve_order hazard and uncovered by the coverage the judge's finding forced into existence. mjs laneRecordFrom (state.mjs:1638) builds `{...defaultLaneRecord(feature), ...parsed}`, and a JS spread over an existing key overwrites IN PLACE rather than reordering -- so the emitted order is the DEFAULT's. The Rust `State` struct declares `phase` before `feature`/`mode` because that is defaultState()'s order for state.json, while defaultLaneRecord puts `feature, mode` before `phase`. The port emitted {schema_version, phase, feature, mode, ...} against mjs's {schema_version, feature, mode, phase, ...}.
deviations.blast_radius: status's `lanes` block, in both the default summary (the ACTIVE lane, serialized in full) and the --lanes-full array. It was invisible until now for two compounding reasons: --status-check never ran --lanes-full, and the harness inherited the ambient CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, which resolved to a session with no record in the fixture, so `active` was always null on a developer machine. Building the row explicitly also removes the `workers` deletion entirely -- the honest fix is never to emit a key defaultLaneRecord does not declare, not to emit and then remove it.
deviations.proven_by: bee-parity --status-check legs enriched/json (5266 bytes) and enriched/json+lanes-full (5223 bytes), both zero diff against the frozen mjs; plus plain/json+lanes-full (3284 bytes). Red-first verified by reverting to struct-order serialization: mjs {schema_version, feature, mode, phase} vs rust {schema_version, phase, feature, mode}.
deviations.scope: crates/bee-core/src/state.rs -- same out-of-glob justification as above.

deviations.what: crates/bee-parity/src/runner.rs now clears CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and sets BEE_SESSION_ID explicitly per scenario for every spawned leg, instead of inheriting the parent environment.
deviations.why: resolveSessionId (claims.mjs:139) reads BEE_SESSION_ID then CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID from the ambient environment, and buildLaneSummary uses the result to decide whether there is an active lane to serialize in full. Inheriting the environment made the harness's BRANCH COVERAGE depend on who ran it: under a Claude Code session, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is set to an id with no session record in the fixture, so `active` resolved to null and no full lane record was ever serialized -- silently, and only on developer machines. Parity itself was never at risk (both runtimes read the same env), but the proof quietly shrank, which is how the lane-row ordering bug above survived a green run.
deviations.proven_by: assert_enriched_signature now requires a FULL lane record in the payload (`"active":{"schema_version"` for the summary legs, `"lanes":[{"schema_version"` for --lanes-full) plus `"bound_sessions":["parity-live-session"]` on BOTH runtimes, so the harness fails loudly if the active-lane path ever stops being exercised rather than silently proving less.
deviations.scope: crates/bee-parity/* -- inside the cell's files glob.

deviations.what: Relaxed crates/bee-parity/src/rootsafety.rs::assert_structural_safety to accept a `.git` DIRECTORY at a fixture root, while newly refusing a `.git` FILE.
deviations.why: rust-port-4's verify (bee-parity --self-check) had been RED on main since rust-port-19 landed: that cell deliberately grew real git ancestry into the D5 fixture, putting a `.git` directory at the fixture root, and the old check refused any `.git` at all (observed: `root-safety: /tmp/bee-parity-leg-a-... contains a .git`). This cell's truth 5 requires --self-check to still pass, so the red had to be repaired, not routed around. What B5 protects is 'this root resolves to ITSELF, never the repo live store', which still holds -- queen-bench/src/fixture.rs's own module docs state resolveRootsCore's git-root fallback resolves storeRoot === workRoot === the fixture root. The check is now TIGHTER in the case that matters: a `.git` FILE (the linked-worktree marker, whose resolution really does walk out to another checkout's store) is refused, which the old code never distinguished.
deviations.proven_by: bee-parity --self-check exits 0. Two unit tests: rejects_dot_git_file_marker_at_root, accepts_dot_git_directory_at_root.
deviations.scope: crates/bee-parity/* -- inside the cell's files glob. The CI blind spot that let a red rust-port-4 verify sit unnoticed on main was filed separately by the orchestrator as its own backlog row.

deviations.kind: scope addition beyond the cell's letter
deviations.what: Added a second parity scenario, `enriched` (crates/bee-parity/src/enrich.rs), and a third leg `--lanes-full`, so --status-check runs 2 scenarios x 3 legs instead of 1 x 2.
deviations.why: The cell asked for a --status-check arm over the D5 fixture and did not ask for a second store shape. But that fixture is pinned for SIZE and deliberately quiet in SHAPE: phase idle, no feature/mode/lanes/handoff/contention, no configured commands or models, gates all pending. A proof over it alone would have left the bypass banner, the Lanes line, the contention block, recommended_next's handoff branch, formatSlot's cli and model@effort shapes, and the capture-queue / PBI / tier-mix / staleness lines unproven -- a byte-parity claim with a large silent hole. That hole was not hypothetical: the lane-row key-order bug above lived in it. Enrichment only ADDS input records to a clone; mjs remains the sole oracle in both scenarios, nothing is normalized or allowed, and the bench's own fixture is never touched.
deviations.proven_by: Six legs, all zero diff: plain/json 3339 B, plain/text 1549 B, plain/json+lanes-full 3284 B, enriched/json 5266 B, enriched/text 2542 B, enriched/json+lanes-full 5223 B. Each scenario carries its own content-pinned seeded mutation, asserted on the stdout diff specifically.
deviations.scope: crates/bee-parity/* -- inside the cell's files glob. The D5 fixture generator was not modified and not shrunk.
